purpose:
Authorisation to Release Funds from the Armed Forces
Community Fund - July 2026
content:
Authorisation to Release Funds from the Armed Forces
Community Fund - July 2026

That the following Armed Forces Community fund
grant award totalling £545 is approved
 
Swaffham Town Council - £545
Funding will support traffic management for the Norfolk Royal
British Legion County Standard Rededication Service in Swaffham on
Sunday 6 September 2026. Swaffham has been chosen to host this
prestigious annual event, one of the most important occasions in
the Royal British Legion calendar in Norfolk. The £545 grant
will be used solely for traffic management costs for the service;
no other project costs are included. Norfolk County Council has
confirmed the road closure will be authorised at no cost.
 

This event offers organisations and members of
the Armed Forces Community a supportive space to remember fallen
comrades through the Act of Remembrance, while raising awareness of
the RBL's modern mission. By bringing together local veteran
charities, civic leaders, and residents, attendees can easily
access help and connect with others in the community.
 

None

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To seek Cabinet approval to undertake public
consultation on the Regulation 19 draft Local Plan, the Integrated
Assessment and the Habitats Regulations Assessment) for a period of
just over 6 weeks.
content:
To seek Cabinet approval to undertake public
consultation on the Regulation 19 draft Local Plan, the Integrated
Assessment and the Habitats Regulations Assessment) for a period of
just over 6 weeks.

RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
Cabinet approves the
Draft Local Plan (Regulation 19) as set out in Appendix 1 to this
Report;
 
2)   
Cabinet agrees that
the Draft Plan included at Appendix 1 and the Policies Map,
available via a web-link at, are published for consultation for a
period of at least 6 weeks;
 
3)   
Cabinet notes the
Integrated Assessment and the Habitats Regulations Assessment:
Executive Summary of the Plan (and the other documents available in
the ‘Examination Library’ on the Council’s
website);
 
4)   
Cabinet agrees that
the Integrated Assessment (incorporating Sustainability Appraisal
and Strategic Environmental Assessment requirements) and the
Habitats Regulations Assessment will also be the subject of formal
consultation for the same period;
 
5)   
Cabinet endorses the
Consultation Strategy set out as Appendix 3 to this
Report;
 
6)   
Cabinet agrees that
the Council will also consider comments that might be made on any
other elements of the Local Plan Evidence Base;
 
7)   
Cabinet grants
delegated authority to the Director of Planning and Building
Control, in consultation with the Leader of the Council to make any
necessary typographical or other non-material changes to Appendix 1
prior to publication for consultation; and
 
8)   
Cabinet notes that the
draft Plan (if approved) would be a material consideration in the
determination of planning (and other relevant) applications –
and would be accorded the weight appropriate to the stage it has
reached in the plan making process as set out in the National
Planning Policy Framework

The Draft Local Plan proposed at Appendix 1 builds on the
extensive community
engagement that has been ongoing throughout the Local Plan
process and sets out
an updated full draft Local Plan (from that consulted upon
at the Regulation 18 phase
in October to December 2025). The new draft Plan
incorporates a series of
development management policies and proposals for strategic
development and
sustainable growth across the District.
 
The preparation of a Local Plan is a statutory requirement
and must follow a statutory
procedure, including public consultation and examination.
If the Council were to
pursue a different approach, overall preparation of a
new Local Plan for Breckland
would be substantially delayed leading to potential risk in
the ongoing management
and delivery of development in the District. Regard also needs to be given
to
proposed changes in the Local Plan process, which the
Council would need to
undertake if it misses the date of 31st December 2026 for
submission to the Planning
Inspectorate.
 
Recommendations 1 and 3 relate to the Plan and the proposed
consultation.
 
The recommendations (two and four) also relate to the two
Assessments that will
ensure the Council complies with regulatory provisions
associated with Sustainability
Appraisal / Strategic Environmental Assessment / Habitats
Regulations.
 
The 5th recommendation relates to the rest of the evidence
base.
 
The 6th recommendation relates to the consultation process
planned if the main
recommendations (1 to 4) are agreed.
 
The 7th – recommendation provides some
‘editing’ ability (of Appendix 1) for
officers
in period from Cabinet through to the start of the
consultation period.
 
The final – 8th – recommendation –
provides clarity as to the weight that should be
given to the draft Plan – within the application
determination process - at this stage
of the Plan making process.
 
Expected Benefits
 
The Government expects local councils to have up-to-date
Local Plans to guide
development in their area. This Plan means that – if
it is ultimately adopted - the
Council would retain control over where development should
be located rather than
be at risk from unplanned speculative development,
sometimes without sufficient
benefit to local communities. Failure to have an up-to-date
plan could also risk
government intervention and result in a loss of local
control.

OPTIONS
 
1)   
The main recommended
approach is for Cabinet to agree the
proposed Draft Local Plan included at
Appendix 1 of this report for consultation, provide delegated
authority for minor amendments to the Plan ahead of its publication
for consultation and agree to a minimum six
week consultation period on the Plan.
 
2)   
Alternatively, Cabinet
could decide not to undertake consultation on the draft Local Plan
included at Appendix 1 and request substantial amendments to the
Plan or seek a different approach. However, that would almost
certainly delay the start of the consultation and put at greater
risk the likelihood of the Council being able to submit the Plan
prior to the end of the year. If the Plan isn’t submitted by
then then the Council would need to restart the whole Local Plan
process – under a new set of national Regulations.
 
3)   
The other
recommendations being put forward tend to flow from the
consideration of whether or not to consult on the Plan – i.e.
if the decision on that is to go ahead then Page 19 of 22 the other
recommendations flow from that – whereas if the decision were
to be to not consult then the other recommendations become rather
irrelevant.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for public consultation on the Regulation 19 draft Local Plan, Integrated Assessment, and Habitats Regulations Assessment.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To seek approval to
undertake a ‘Call for Sites’ exercise to invite anyone
with land with the potential to develop for gypsy and traveller
sites to submit to the Council for consideration as part of the
Local Plan process.
content:
To seek approval to
undertake a ‘Call for Sites’ exercise to invite anyone
with land with the potential to develop for gypsy and traveller
sites to submit to the Council for consideration as part of the
Local Plan process.

RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
Cabinet approves the
Call for Sites forms and accompanying guidance.
 
2)   
Cabinet approves a
call for sites engagement period
starting on the 31st July and ending on
the 16th September.
 
3)   
Cabinet grants
delegated authority to the Director of Planning and Building
Control, in consultation with the Leader of the Council to make any
necessary typographical or other minor changes to the papers prior
to publication for consultation.

The Preparation of a Local Plan is a
statutory requirement and must follow a statutory procedure,
including public consultation and examination.
 
In order
to demonstrate that the Council is doing all that it can to
meet the needs of Gypsies, Travellers
and Travelling Show people an additional
call for site is recommended to seek to
meet that need. Following the visit from the Planning Inspector to
assist with the Plan being found sound at examination additional
efforts to meet the needs of this group should be undertaken. The
benefits are not only related to the Local Plan and adoption, if
successful suitable sites could be identified to meet the need of
this community for the coming years.
 
The government expects local councils to
have up-to-date Local Plans to guide development in their area.
This plan means that the Council can retain control over where
development should be located rather than unplanned speculative
development, sometimes without sufficient benefit to local
communities. Failure to have an up-to-date plan could risk
government intervention and result in a loss of local
control.

Option 1
(Recommended)
It is considered that this focused call for sites is the
best way to bring forward land that is suitable for Gypsy and
Travellers and while only one site previously came forward it is
hoped with some additional advertising additional sites could be
put forward by landowners.
 
Option 2
There is the option for the Council not to undertake the
call for sites however it is considered that this will reduce the
soundness of the plan at examination stage given the lack of
available Gypsy and Traveller sites.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a 'Call for Sites' exercise to identify potential land for gypsy and traveller sites in the Local Plan process.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To seek Cabinet
approval for the revised Local Development Scheme.
content:
To seek Cabinet
approval for the revised Local Development Scheme.
 

RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
Cabinet approves the
Local Development Scheme July 2026 for the Full Update of the Local
plan.
 
2)   
Cabinet grants
delegated authority to the Director of Planning and Building
Control, in consultation with the Leader of the Council to make any
necessary typographical or other non-material changes to the Local
Development Scheme prior to publication.
 
3)   
Cabinet grant
delegated authority to the Director of Planning and Building
Control, in consultation with the Leader of the Council to formally
replace the Local Development Scheme March 2025, to take effect
from the date of publication of the Local Development Scheme July
2026.
 
4)   
Cabinet grant
delegated authority to the Director of Planning and Building
Control, in consultation with the Leader of the Council to submit
the updated Local Development Scheme to the Ministry of Housing
Communities and Local Government (MHCLG).

The LDS is being updated to amend the
timeframe of the Local Plan. The current LDS sets the timeframe for
the Local Plan at 2024 to 2042. The
revised timeline is 2025 to 2043. By moving the start date of the
Local Plan we are
able to use, in accordance with the NPPF, the most up to
date information available. When a Local Plan is adopted, it
should, in accordance with paragraph 22 of the NPPF include
strategic policies which look ahead over a ‘minimum
15 year period from adoption’.
While the LDS timetables that the Local Plan is set to be submitted
for examination December 2026 at this stage the timetable for
adoption is with the Planning Inspectorate. There are likely to be
a considerable number of Local Plans submitted in 2026 given the
changes to the plan making system with all plans submitted under
the ‘legacy’ system having to be submitted by the
31st December 2026. It is therefore
possible that the Plan will not be ready for adoption at full
council until 2028 as there may be delays in getting through
examination owing to the Inspectorates workload. As such, to seek
to put the plan in the best position possible the amendments to the
timetable are recommended.

Breckland Local Development Scheme
2026 and the timetable set on the LDS
2026.

decision_maker: Cllr Tristan Ashby, Executive Member for Health and Communities
purpose:
Health and Wellbeing Public Health Funding £100k
26/27
content:
Health and Wellbeing Public Health Funding £100k
26/27

To agree funding received on behalf of the Breckland Health
& Wellbeing Partnership to be distributed in accordance with
partnership governance.  Decisions will
be made in line with the Breckland Health & Wellbeing Strategy
2025 – 2028.
 

A
Health & Wellbeing Partnership (HWP) is a group of
organisations that work together to improve the health and
wellbeing of a particular community or population.  These partnerships form part of the statutory
makeup of Integrated Care systems and may involve a variety of
stakeholders, such as public health agencies, community-based
organisations, healthcare providers, schools, businesses and local
government.  HWPs can take many forms,
and the specific goals and activities of a partnership may vary
depending on the needs of the community it serves.
 
Norfolk and Suffolk 8 x HWPs, which align to district
council boundaries, were officially launched in July 2022 as part
of the new legislation for the Integrated Care System. The
Norfolk-based HWPs aim to address challenges that no single
organisation can address alone, they will collectively drive
strategies and activities for their place to:
 

Promote the health & wellbeing of
residents.
Address the wider determinants of
health.
Tackle health inequalities
Prioritise the prevention agenda.
Align, develop and influence NHS and local
government services and commissioning.

 
HWPs have been formed to collectively drive strategies and
activities which address root causes of health inequalities at a
local level.  Each HWP has developed a
Local Strategy & Delivery Plan for their partnership and
funding provided by Norfolk County Council, NHS and other statutory
partners underpins this Local Strategy and Delivery
Plan.
 
Breckland Council may act as ‘holders’ of
funding but cannot distribute it without the approval of membership
of Breckland Health & Wellbeing Partnership.  All funding decisions will be documented and where
applicable, formal proposals recorded.
 
So far, identified funding comprises: £100,000 from
April 2026 – March 2027 and subsequent years up until March
2028.

None.
topline: The Cllr Tristan Ashby has decided to distribute £100k in public health funding to the Breckland Health & Wellbeing Partnership.

decision_maker: General Purposes Committee
purpose:
To seek approval to increase the cleaning
establishment within the Property Service by 2 x 15-hour satellite
cleaner roles to support operational delivery across council
sites.
content:
To seek approval to increase the cleaning
establishment within the Property Service by 2 x 15-hour satellite
cleaner roles to support operational delivery across council
sites.

RESOLVED that:
 
The approval of the addition of 2 x 15-hour
satellite cleaner posts within the Property Service
establishment.
 


1)   
Ensuring Effective Resourcing
Maintaining a safe, clean, and
compliant environment across all operational buildings is a core
responsibility of the Property Service. Adequate in-house resource
is essential to deliver this consistently, minimise reliance on
costly external contractors, and ensure the Council retains control
over standards and service delivery.
 

2)   
Supporting Service Resilience and Flexibility
Additional resource will
provide the flexibility needed to manage staff absences due to
annual leave or sickness and respond to periods of increased
demand. This will reduce the need for reactive short-term solutions
and enable a more predictable and resilient service.
 

3)   
Maximising Operational Control and Efficiency
Bringing cleaning provision
in-house has already demonstrated improvements in quality,
oversight, and operational control. Expanding this capability will
allow the Property Service to maintain consistent standards across
all sites, particularly residential properties, while also offering
the potential to generate additional income from tenant cleans.
This proposal is expected to
deliver significant operational and financial benefits, including
reduced costs through less reliance on external contractors,
greater control and oversight of cleaning standards across all
sites, and enhanced flexibility and resilience to manage staff
absences or increased demand. It will maintain consistently high
standards of cleanliness, reduce pressure on existing staff, and
provide the opportunity to generate additional income by offering
cleaning services to commercial tenants.
 


1)   
Do Nothing
 

2)

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To seek Cabinet approval for the adoption of
the Breckland Procurement and Contract Management Strategy 2026
– 2028
content:
To seek Cabinet approval for the adoption of
the Breckland Procurement and Contract Management Strategy 2026
– 2028

RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
the Breckland Procurement and Contract Management Strategy 2026
– 2028 be approved
 
2)   
delegated authority be given to the Deputy Chief Executive, in
consultation with the Executive Member for Property, Projects and
Procurement, to make amendments required to reflect legislative
updates, operational refinements or organisational change.
 
3)   
progress against the strategy be reported annually to Governance
and Audit Committee and bi-annually to the Corporate Management
Team.
 

Adoption of the Strategy will ensure compliance with the
Procurement Act 2023, strengthen governance, oversight and
transparency, embed measurable social value and sustainability
outcomes within procurement activity, improve contract management
practice and performance monitoring, support readiness for Local
Government Reorganisation (LGR), and enhance supplier engagement
while increasing local spend where appropriate. Approval of the
Breckland Procurement and Contract Management Strategy 2026 - 2028
is recommended to ensure the council has a clear, modern and
legally compliant framework for commissioning, procurement and
contract management.
 
The strategy strengthens governance, embeds the
requirements of the Procurement Act 2023, and positions procurement
as a strategic enabler of the Corporate Plan priorities. It
improves transparency, supports delivery of measurable social value
and environmental outcomes, enhances contract performance
oversight, and increases local economic impact. Adoption will also
strengthen the Council's readiness for local government
reorganisation by ensuring that robust contract records, risk
management and transition planning are in place, thereby protecting
service continuity and financial resilience.


1)   
That Cabinet approves the Breckland Procurement and Contract
Management Strategy 2026 - 2028. Delegates authority to the Deputy
Chief Executive, in consultation with the Executive Member for
Property, Projects and Procurement, to make amendments required to
reflect legislative updates, operational refinements or
organisational change. Notes that progress against the strategy
will be reported annually to Governance and Audit Committee and
bi-annually to the Corporate Management team.
 

2)   
Do Nothing (Not Recommended): Without a formal Procurement
and Contract Management Strategy, the Council would continue to
operate without a clear framework aligned to the Procurement Act
2023 and LGR requirements. This creates significant legal,
compliance, and reputational risks, reduces transparency, limits
the ability to demonstrate value for money, and prevents embedding
social value, sustainability, and improved contract management
practices..
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Breckland Procurement and Contract Management Strategy 2026-2028.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To provide a grant to enable delivery of a
young person’s transitional housing scheme in Breckland.
content:
To provide a grant to enable delivery of a
young person’s transitional housing scheme in Breckland.

RESOLVED that:
 

1)   
Cabinet approve the award of a £1.2m capital grant to YMCA
Norfolk to support the delivery of a new young person’s
transitional housing scheme in the district, subject to compliance
with the Subsidy Control Act 2022.
 

2)   
delegated authority be given to Sarah Shipley, Assistant Director
for Health and Housing in consultation with the Executive Member to
finalise and enter into the Grant Funding Agreement with YMCA
Norfolk and to complete all necessary arrangements for compliance
with the Subsidy Control Act 2022.
 

REASONS:
 
Identified need and service gap: There
is a demonstrable and ongoing need for supported accommodation for
young people aged 18–25, including those presenting as
homeless and those leaving care. Breckland’s Housing Strategy
(September 2024) and analysis of the housing register have
identified a gap in provision of young people’s transitional
housing in the district.
 
Prevention of homelessness and improved
outcomes: A supported housing scheme would contribute to
homelessness prevention, reduce repeat presentations, and provide
structured support to enable young people to develop skills,
stability and resilience, improving longer-term housing
outcomes.
 
Funding opportunity and value for
money: The Council has already ringfenced £1.2m within
the capital programme for the purposes of an affordable housing
scheme. A grant can be used to lever in additional investment from
YMCA Norfolk and Homes England Affordable Homes Programme funding
(subject to eligibility and approvals). This creates an opportunity
to maximise delivery and value for money through a blended funding
approach.
 
Expertise and deliverability: YMCA
Norfolk is an established provider with relevant expertise in
delivering and managing supported housing schemes for young
people.
 
Strategic alignment and legacy: The
scheme aligns with the Council’s strategic housing objectives
and reflects an opportunity for strong cross-organisational
working, creating a positive legacy project for young people in the
district, particularly in the context of forthcoming Local
Government Reorganisation.
 
The Breckland Housing Strategy identifies four
priorities to meeting the districts’ housing need, and this
proposal would meet two of these priorities for our residents:
 
·        
Priority 1: Increase the supply and diversity of affordable housing
to ensure the right types of housing are available in the right
places.
·        
Priority 4: Support vulnerable residents to access suitable homes
and have housing choice.
 
The ‘Do nothing’ option does not
address housing need: The option of taking no action would not
address the identified service gap, would maintain pressure on
temporary accommodation and housing resources, and would miss the
opportunity to progress a preventative housing pathway for
vulnerable young people.
 


1)   
Approve the award of a £1.2m capital grant to YMCA Norfolk to
support the delivery of a new young person’s transitional
housing scheme in the district, subject to compliance with the
Subsidy Control Act 2022.
 

2)   
Delegate authority to Sarah Shipley, Assistant Director for Health
and Housing in consultation with the Executive Member to finalise
and enter into the Grant Funding Agreement with YMCA Norfolk and to
complete all necessary arrangements for compliance with the Subsidy
Control Act 2022.
 

3)   
Do nothing
topline: The Cabinet has decided to provide a £1.2m capital grant to YMCA Norfolk for a young person's transitional housing scheme in Breckland.

To adopt "make" the Yaxham Neighbourhood Plan
Review as part of the Statutory Development Plan for Breckland and
update the Breckland District Policies Map with the relevant
policies.

RESOLVED that:
 

1)   
the Yaxham Neighbourhood Plan Review, as written at
the time of the Referendum, is “made” as part of the
Statutory Development Plan for Breckland Council, as required by
paragraph (4)(a) of section 38A of the 2004 Planning and Compulsory
Purchase Act (Option1) be confirmed.
 

2)   
this decision be published as required by paragraph
(9) of section 38A 2004 Planning and Compulsory Purchase
Act.
 
3)   
Yaxham Parish Council and any other prescribed
persons be advised of this decision to meet the requirements of
paragraph (10) of section 38A of the 2004 Planning and Compulsory
Purchase Act; and
 
Recommend to Full
Council to amend the Breckland District Policies Map to
meet the requirements of paragraph 9 Town and Country (Local
Planning) (England) Regulations 2012.

It is recommended that members endorse Option
1 as there was a positive vote 95% in favour for
‘making’ the Yaxham
Neighbourhood Plan Review through a Referendum following an
independent examination and there is considered to be compliance
with European obligations and Human Rights conventions.
 
The main benefit to “making” or
agreeing the Yaxham Neighbourhood Plan
Review is that it is the final stage in the production of the Plan
and will confirm that it forms part of the statutory
“Development Plan”, thereby continue to allow the
policies to be used in the determination of planning applications
in the Neighbourhood Area.
 



1)   
Cabinet agrees to “make” the Yaxham Neighbourhood Plan Review and is therefore
“adopted” as part of the statutory Development Plan for
Breckland Council, as required by paragraph (4)(a) of section 38A
of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 as
“…more than half of those voting to have voted in
favour of the plan …”, and to undertake the required
publication, advise the Parish Council and other prescribed persons
and subsequently update the District Policies Map.
 
2)   
Council does not make the Yaxham
Neighbourhood Plan Review where “…it
considers that the Plan would breach or would otherwise be
incompatible with any EU obligation or any of the Convention Rights
(within the meaning of the Human Rights Act 1998).”

purpose:
To extend the contract with Xantura Limited
for the implementation and licensing of a homelessness prevention
system for a further 12-month period.
content:
To extend the contract with Xantura Limited
for the implementation and licensing of a homelessness prevention
system for a further 12-month period.

The initial contract term expired on 31 March
2026 and there is provision within the contract to extend for a
further 12-month period.
 
The cost of the extension will be
£163,000 of which £62,000 will be funded by partnership
funding secured through our Inspiring Communities
Programme.  The remaining £101,000
will be funded from underspends on the 2025/26 budget and the
Leader and Chief Executive had delegated authority from Council to
authorise allocation of these underspends (February 2026).
 
Breckland Council, like many councils, is
still experiencing high numbers of people who are presenting as
homeless.
 
The system that has been procured will - using
a wide range of data from across the Local Authority, Commissioned
Services and wider third-party partners - provide functionality
that will support the Council’s Housing Team in identifying
those Breckland residents that are most likely to present as
homeless or at imminent risk of becoming homeless.
 
In doing so, the system will enable targeted
interventions to be made – using early intervention
principles – and to reduce overall demand on council services
(and the cost of said services).
 
Significant due diligence was undertaken
before commencing the original procurement with site visits and
meetings with a number of different local authorities and solution
providers.
 
Much of the data sharing and system
preparation work has been completed and it will go live for active
use by the Housing Team in June 2026.
 
Extending the Contract also allows further
work to be done exploring how the system can be used more widely to
support council services as part of our Inspiring Communities
Programme.
 
The original procurement was run through the G
Cloud framework and Xantura submitted
the successful tender.
 

To extend the contract with Xantura Limited for the implementation and
licensing of a homelessness prevention system.

N/A

decision_maker: Cllr Phil Cowen, Executive Member for Finance, Revenue and Benefits
purpose: Debt Management Policy - 3 yearly review
content:
Debt Management Policy - 3 yearly review

That the Corporate Debt
Management and Recovery Policy be approved
 

This is a three yearly refresh of the existing
policy.
 
To continue to provide a clear policy and
procedure to manage the recovery of Council debt.
 
Effective debt management is crucial to the
success of any organisation. It is essential that this Council has
clear policies and procedures to manage the recovery of debt. If
the Council is to achieve its aim of effective income management,
then it must seek to recover all debts due, and sustain collection
rates.  This policy has been designed to
address these aims.
 
The corporate debt management & recovery
policy was originally approved at Cabinet in April 2017 and since
that time is formally reviewed every 3 years to ensure that it
remains up to date and appropriate for the Council and reflects
latest working practices.  The Anglia
Revenues Partnership (ARP) have their own policy for the recovery
of their areas of debt; Council Tax, Business Rates (NNDR),
Discretionary Housing Payments, Enforcement Fees and Housing
Benefit Overpayments and therefore this policy does not cover
ARP.
 
In reviewing and updating this policy we have
consulted with ARP, Planning, Legal services and Property
departments and have incorporated their responses where
necessary.
 
There have been very few changes in the last 3
years, so the policy remains relatively unchanged.  The minor updates include:

Amending references to
Bailiffs to Enforcement to reflect updated
language
Amending reference to county
court bailiff to County Court or High court to reflect
updated names

 


·        
To approve the
Corporate Debt Management and Recovery Policy

·        
Not to approve the
Corporate Debt Management and Recovery Policy
topline: The Cllr Phil Cowen has decided to approve the Corporate Debt Management and Recovery Policy after a three yearly review.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To set out Breckland's proposals to grow its
support for the Armed Forces Community, including a new grant
funding scheme.
content:
RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
Cabinet notes the success that Breckland has had in supporting the
Armed Forces Community within the district.
 
2)   
Cabinet endorses the proposed Programme of Support for the Armed
Forces Community as set out in Appendix A
 
3)   
Cabinet establishes the Armed Forces Community Fund as set out in
the proposed Prospectus in Appendix B
 
4)   
Cabinet delegates authority to the Executive Member for Economic
Development &Growth, in consultation with the Assistant
Director for Economic Development, to assess and approve grant
applications.
 

Breckland Council should be proud of the
positive work that has been delivered in support of the Armed
Forces Community, and the recommendations allow the Council to go
build upon this work and achieve even more.
 
The Programme of Support sets out a positive
vision as to how support for the Armed Forces Community can be
expanded within the district, ensuring that residents, as well as
employees from the Community, are supported.
 
An Armed Forces Community Fund would allow
Breckland to fund activity within the district that supports the
Armed Forces Community and raises awareness of the contributions
that they make.
 
Previous funding schemes that have been
centred around specific anniversaries in the Armed Forces calendar
have been well received. Creation of this Fund would allow
organisations to access funding to deliver projects all year round
and not tied to a specific event or anniversary.

Option 1 – That Cabinet notes the
success that Breckland have had in supporting the Armed Forces
Community, endorses the proposed Programme of Support and
establishes the Armed Forces Community Fund
 
Option 2 -Do Nothing – Meaning
that the proposed Programme of Support is not approved and the
Armed Forces Community Fund is not established.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to establish an Armed Forces Community Fund and endorse a Programme of Support for the Armed Forces Community in Breckland.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To seek Cabinet approval to commence immediate
and focused work to develop the evidence base and policy
justification required to determine whether it is appropriate to
introduce an Article 4 Direction removing permitted development
rights for change of use from Class C3 (dwellinghouses) to Class C4
(small Houses in Multiple Occupation) in parts of the district
where concentrations are undermining community balance.
content:
To seek Cabinet approval to commence immediate
and focused work to develop the evidence base and policy
justification required to determine whether it is appropriate to
introduce an Article 4 Direction removing permitted development
rights for change of use from Class C3 (dwellinghouses) to Class C4
(small Houses in Multiple Occupation) in parts of the district
where concentrations are undermining community balance.

RESOLVED that:
 

1)   
Cabinet approves the commencement of a comprehensive and focused
evidence-gathering and policy development programme to support the
potential introduction of an Article 4 Direction removing permitted
development rights for change of use from Class C3 to Class C4 in
areas where concentration is undermining community balance.
 

2)   
Cabinet request that Officers report back with detailed findings
and recommendations.
 

The Council has concerns regarding the
cumulative impact of increasing HMO concentrations in specific
areas within the District.
 
Residents have expressed concerns about:
 

·        
The erosion of established residential character

·        
The incremental loss of traditional family housing

·        
Pressures on local infrastructure

·        
The destabilising effect of high-turnover occupancy patterns
 
It is therefore considered to be appropriate
and necessary to examine whether the continuation of national
permitted development rights in specified locations is compatible
with the Council’s duty to promote balanced, stable and
sustainable communities.

Option 1: Take no action and retain
existing permitted development arrangements, accepting that the
Council would continue to have no planning control over new Class
C3 to C4 changes of use.
 
Option 2 (Recommended): Commence
immediate and focused work to develop the robust evidence base
required to determine whether national permitted development rights
are resulting in wholly unacceptable adverse impacts in defined
areas of the District, with a view to returning to Cabinet with a
proposed non-immediate Article 4 Direction if justified
topline: The Cabinet has decided to commence work on potentially introducing an Article 4 Direction to address concerns about the impact of increasing Houses in Multiple Occupation concentrations on community balance.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To approve the submitted Business Plan for the
forthcoming period
content:
To approve the submitted Business Plan for the
forthcoming period

That Cabinet:
 
recommends to Council to
re-approve the Breckland Bridge Ltd Business Plan for 2023 -
2028.

Breckland Bridge was created over 10 years ago
with an ambition to create financial returns for its shareholders,
and by default, for the Breckland taxpayer. To that end it has been
successful – over £3.5 million has been generated for
the residents of Breckland through a variety of housing,
commercial, regeneration and land-related projects; building where
the private sector could not, providing affordable homes where some
developers would not, and acting as an exemplar in environmental
standards as well as home building quality, punching above its
weight in terms of size and reach.
 
It is prudent for the Council to review its
position and involvement in the Breckland Bridge joint venture
given the current proposals for Local Government Reorganisation in
Norfolk combined with current prevailing market conditions. The
challenges with the Colkirk scheme demonstrate the risks that can
be experienced in undertaking construction and development,
alongside the potential benefits of such activities. Nonetheless,
the completion of this scheme, including its associated affordable
housing, demonstrate our commitment to our communities and the need
for housing now within the district. These risks are constantly
monitored by the Breckland Bridge board of directors.
 
The Business Plan as presented, aims to
maximise value on existing sites where possible whether for
development or for disposal, delivering the best possible returns
whilst minimising risks to the council as the shareholder.

Option 1: Cabinet recommends to Council
to re-approve the Breckland Bridge Ltd Business Plan for
2023-2028.
 
Option 2: Cabinet does not recommend to
Council to re-approve the Breckland Bridge Ltd Business Plan for
2023-2028.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To review the finance, performance and project
metrics for the council
content:
Councillor Webb, Executive Member for Customer
and Corporate Services, presented the report that provided information and overview of the Council’s
forecast Financial position, Performance and Corporate Projects for
the period 1st September to 31st December 2025 (Q3).
 
Councillor Webb introduced the
performance section of the report and advised that the majority of
key performance indicators were in or near target. She updated
Members on customer contact performance, noting that the Contact
Centre had experienced a challenging period earlier in the year,
which had impacted customer satisfaction scores. However,
improvement had been seen across Quarter 3, particularly in
December, which recorded the strongest monthly performance since
April 2025. Work remained ongoing to ensure continued stability and
sustained improvement.
 
Councillor Webb also
highlighted performance in relation to Freedom of Information (FOI)
requests. Whilst this remained a comparatively strong area for the
Council, Quarter 3 had been challenging due to staff sickness and
increasing complexity in the nature of requests and associated
appeals. She reminded Members that FOI legislation required all
requests to be treated equally, regardless of source. During the
quarter, Officers responded to 152 FOI requests, many of which were
complex and time-consuming. Additional context was provided,
including that the highest number of requests from a single
individual was 7, 18 requests related to matters outside the
Council’s responsibility, and 8 concerned a single location.
To ease pressure on resources, work was underway to publish more
frequently requested information online to reduce the need for
formal FOI submissions.
 
Councillor Hewett presented the
projects update, advising that the Council’s high priority
projects were in a strong position at the end of Quarter 3, with
the majority rated green and progressing as planned. A number of
projects had been completed and formally closed during the period,
delivering measurable benefits to residents.
 
He highlighted progress at the
Attleborough Leisure site, where works were well underway to
improve facilities, alongside the addition of a new 3G football
pitch. Members were reminded of the success of the 3G facility in
Thetford, which had seen participation increase by over 260%,
underlining the positive impact such investment had on physical and
mental wellbeing.
 
Councillor Hewett also reported
on the completion of the second phase of property acquisitions to
meet growing demand for temporary accommodation. The project had
been delivered under budget and exceeded its original target by 10%
in terms of properties purchased, generating a net saving of over
£300,000. Building on this success, the Council was
progressing a further initiative to provide housing and support for
young people leaving the care system.
 
Councillor Cowen presented the
Quarter 3 financial position, referring Members to the detailed
appendices within the report. He noted that the Council continued
to operate in a period of significant uncertainty and change across
local government. Earlier reductions in planning application income
had been reversed, with Quarter 3 showing a significant improvement
in planning fee income.
 
In addition, careful treasury
management and higher interest rates had enabled the Council to
maintain strong returns on its investment portfolio. While some
service pressures remained, the forecast revenue outturn position
showed a positive variance of £657,000, reflecting proactive
financial management and income performance. Councillor Cowen
concluded that the figures demonstrated the Council’s
continued financial stability and ability to deliver its
priorities.
 
 
 
Options
 

1)   
To note the content of the report and appendices
showing detail of Finance, Performance and Corporate
Projects.
 
Reasons for
recommendation
 
To
provide timely information to Members on the overall financial
position of the Council, enabling resource re-allocation to
priorities where necessary and protecting the General fund
balance.

To show
the council’s projects and performance in line with the
reporting criteria set out in the performance framework and the
projects framework.
 
 
RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
The content of the report and appendices showing
detail of Finance, Performance and Corporate Projects be
noted.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To seek authority for the Assistant Director
of Property & infrastructure to dispose of Breckland owned
assets below market value provided there is a social, economic, or
community value.
content:
RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
Agree to give delegated authority to the Assistant Director for
Property and Projects for Breckland District Council (BDC) in
conjunction with the Executive Member for Property, Projects &
Procurement, to transfer assets at an under value where the
attributed value for the asset is £10,000 or less and where
there is clear and demonstrable social, economic, or community
benefit in accordance with the Secretary of State’s General
Consent Order and the Community Asset Transfer Policy
 

Agreeing to permit disposals of BDC-owned
assets at less than best consideration, where there is clear and
demonstrable social, economic and/or community benefit, will enable
the Council to maximise the overall public value derived from its
land and property holdings. In many cases, the long-term benefits
to local communities arising from local ownership and management
outweigh the limited capital receipt that might otherwise be
achieved through disposal at market value.
 
Enabling disposals at an undervalue supports
the Council’s strategic objectives by empowering Town and
Parish Councils and community organisations to take on greater
responsibility for assets that are of local importance. This can
result in improved stewardship, increased community use, and more
sustainable long-term management of assets that might otherwise be
underutilised or require ongoing Council resources.
 

1)   
Agree to give delegated authority to the Assistant Director for
Property and Projects for Breckland District Council in conjunction
with the Executive Member for Property, Projects & Procurement
for BDC to dispose of land and property assets at less than best
consideration where the attributed value for the asset is
£10,000 or less (except in cases where demonstrable community
benefit will arise on certain sites valued above £10k) and
where there is clear social, economic and/or community benefit, in
accordance with the Secretary of State’s General Disposal
Consent (England) 2003 and the Council’s adopted policies and
governance arrangements.
 
2)   
Do nothing – retain requirement for market value
disposals.
Do not agree to disposals at an undervalue and require that all
land and property assets are disposed of at or above market value,
irrespective of any wider social, economic or community benefits
that may arise from alternative ownership or management
arrangements.  This option could
preclude the Parish and Town Councils securing the land they wish
for their communities which would be disadvantageous to our
residents and businesses.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to allow the transfer of assets at an under value for social, economic, or community benefit.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Acceptance of grant funding from the Football
Foundation for Attleborough 3G Pitch of up to £1million
content:
Acceptance of grant funding from the Football
Foundation for Attleborough 3G Pitch of up to £1million

RESOLVED that:
 

1)   
Cabinet agree to accept all grant
funding following submission and successful outcome of a Football
Foundation (FF) application (up to £1m) and set up necessary
budgets to spend and proceed with the delivery of this project via
the FF framework.
 
2)   
Cabinet agree to delegate authority to
accept the terms and conditions of the FF grant to the Executive
Member for Leisure in consultation with the Assistant Director
Contract and Operations.
 

3)   
Cabinet agree to contribute up to £50,000 from
reserves to fund the remaining funding gap.
 

The Attleborough Neighbourhood Plan
(2016-2036) has a specific core objective ‘to provide
excellent new and improved sport and leisure facilities for the
community, working with Attleborough Academy and sport and
community clubs and organisation’.
 
Following a community engagement exercise
carried out in the summer of 2023, an online survey highlighted
that 89.1% of all responses indicated that an all-weather pitch was
important to them. 82.3% of all responses came from people already
involved in grass roots sports and 82.4% advised that they would
consider using community facilities at the site with the most
popular sport indicated being football.
 
Other findings from this engagement exercise
showed that the vast majority agreed that availability of more and
better facilities in the town would encourage them to become more
physically active.
 
3G AGP projects delivered with support from FF
grant funding must ensure inclusivity with a large emphasis on
provision for women and girls, and disability football in particular.
 
As well as delivering a high quality 3G AGP
for the community, a dual use site will provide increased usage
throughout school hours.
 
The feasibility report delivered by TRI-Sports
showed a significant increase in participation is expected and has
engaged with local clubs Attleborough Town FC, Morley FC, and
Rocklands FC all willing to become partner clubs if this is
delivered.
 
The delivery of a 3G AGP at the site will also
strengthen the business case for the site, alongside the wider
leisure improvements, making it more attractive to leisure
operators.
 
Failing to proceed with the project.
 
•                   
would see the continuation of high numbers of football matches and
training for both junior and senior local clubs cancelled due to
poor weather conditions and waterlogged pitches with availability
of 3G AGPs limited in the immediate locality of the town.
•                   
There would be an impact to the business case which could cause
significant challenges in procuring a leisure operator to run the
site on a profit share basis.
•                   
It could be considered a missed opportunity to provide a
c.£1.5m facility for minimal capital spend from the
Council

1)   
That Cabinet agree to
accept all grant funding following a FF application (up to
£1m) and set up necessary budgets to spend.
(recommended)
 
2)   
That Cabinet agree to
delegate authority to accept the terms and conditions of the grant
to the Executive Member for Leisure in consultation with the
Assistant Director Contract and Operations (recommended)
 
3)   
That Cabinet agree to
contribute up to £50,000 from reserves to fund the remaining
funding gap (recommended)
 
4)   
Do Nothing
topline: The Cabinet has decided to accept grant funding for the construction of a 3G pitch in Attleborough, following strong community support and engagement.

economic and community benefits, consistent with the Councils
strategic objectives and the requirements of the Secretary of
States General Consent Order.

allowing resources to be redirected to other priority services.

at £Nil, subject to Swaffham Town Council confirming its

to the Executive Member for Property, Projects & Procurement to
finalise the terms and conditions and complete the
transactions.
 

2)   
Agree for BDC to dispose of the car parks at full market value.
 

3)   
Do nothing and retain ownership and responsibility for the car
parks.

decision_maker: Cllr Sam Chapman-Allen, Leader of the Council
purpose: Norfolk Police and Crime Panel Funding
content:
Norfolk Police and Crime Panel Funding

To approve Breckland
Council’s contribution towards any Police and Crime Panel
costs which exceed the Home Office grant for 2025–28. The
total overall additional contribution is to be capped at 20%
of the grant allocation and apportioned between local authorities
as set out in the Panel Arrangements.

The Norfolk Police and Crime Panel is a joint
committee hosted by Norfolk County Council. The Home Office
provides a grant to host authorities to maintain the Panel, and
this allocation has remained unchanged since its establishment in
2012.
 
The grant is now issued under a three-year
agreement, reflecting the government’s plan to end the Police
and Crime Commissioner model in 2028. At that point, governance
functions will transfer to Mayors or local council leaders, and
Police and Crime Panels will be replaced.
 
For the first time, forecast expenditure for
2025–26 is expected to exceed the Home Office grant due to
inflation and pay awards.
 
At its meeting on 28 October 2025, the Panel
considered several savings proposals, but not all were accepted,
resulting in an anticipated overspend.
Norfolk Leaders have agreed in principle that
their councils will contribute towards costs above the Home Office
grant for the current three-year period. They specified that the
total overall additional contribution is to be capped at 20% of the
grant allocation and apportioned between local authorities as set
out in the Panel Arrangements. This decision effects Breckland
Council’s contribution.
 
See attached report
for further details.

Option 1 – (RECOMMENDED)To approve Breckland
Council’s contribution towards any Police and Crime Panel
costs which exceed the Home Office grant for 2025–28. The
total overall additional contribution is to be capped at 20%
of the grant allocation and apportioned between local authorities
as set out in the Panel Arrangements.
Norfolk Leaders considered and rejected the
following alternative options:
 
Option 2 – Do nothing –
Norfolk County Council, as host authority, would need to consider
what steps were required to fund any variance.
 
Option 3 – Consider an
alternative proposal – for example making a smaller reduction
in the Scrutiny Support Officer’s time supporting the Panel
Reducing from the current 3-days to 2.5 days per week (0.5fte)
would still generate savings of approximately £4,139.16 in
2025-26.  Combined with the savings
already agree, this should bring the overall expenditure within the
available grant (an approximate total of £62,969.48) in
2025-26.  Support for Police, Crime and
Fire Panels varies across the country; however, 0.5fte is broadly
comparable as many support officers also undertake other Democratic
Services responsibilities.
topline: The Leader of Breckland Council has decided to approve additional funding for the Norfolk Police and Crime Panel beyond the Home Office grant.

RESOLVED to

1)

purpose of Breckland Bridge Ltd and approve the business plan 2026

position and involvement in the Breckland Bridge joint venture
given the current proposals for Local Government Reorganisation in

be experienced in undertaking construction and development,

monitored by the Breckland Bridge board of directors. To mitigate
any continued risk with undertake development directly it is
prudent to review the approach and vision of the joint venture.
 
The new business plan is supported by both
shareholders and provides a clear direction on the business of the
company for the next period. The business plan aims to maximise
value on existing sites where possible in disposal, delivering the
best possible returns whilst minimising risks to the council as the
shareholder whilst at the same time shielding any future unitary
authority against financial hardship as much as possible.

approve the business plan 2026-2031.

Approve writing off the working capital loan to Breckland Bridge

its subsidiaries).

3)    
Approve the provision of funding to contribute towards the overhead
costs of running Breckland Bridge Ltd and its subsidiaries.
 
Option 2: Cabinet does not recommend to
Council to:

1)    
Approve the new vision and purpose of Breckland Bridge Ltd or
approve the business plan 2026-2031.

2)    
Approve writing off the working capital loan to Breckland Bridge
Ltd and any unpaid Colkirk scheme loans to Breckland Bridge Ltd (or
its subsidiaries).

3)    
Approve the provision of funding to contribute towards the overhead
costs of running Breckland Bridge Ltd and its subsidiaries.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To seek Cabinet's support for Breckland's
approach to Devolution
content:
RESOLVED that:
 
1)   
Cabinet supports a positive vision for devolution, as set out in
the enclosed Executive Policy Statement (Appendix 1) of this
report, and agrees to work with local partners, including the
Norfolk and Suffolk Combined County Authority (NSCCA) a future
Mayor, and national partners to encourage a more ambitious,
long-term aspiration for devolution in the region.
 
2)   
Cabinet endorses the draft Investment Prospectus, as set out in
Appendix 2, and delegates to the Chief Executive, in consultation
with the Leader, the consultation and finalisation of a Prospectus.
To be shared and promoted to the NSCCA alongside any future Mayoral
candidates and the Mayor once elected.
 

Endorsing a longer-term, more
ambitious vision for Devolution in Norfolk and Suffolk will ensure
that the discussion as to how the NSCAA moves onto an
‘Established’ status begins early, and that Breckland
shares its vision as to what a deeper more meaningful form of
Devolution looks like.
 
Access to the investment funds
that accompanies Devolution presents Breckland with opportunities
to support important local priorities. Ensuring that awareness is
raised of the opportunities within Breckland will aid future
applications.
 

Option 1 (Recommended) – To Agree
to the recommendations:
 
1)   
That Cabinet supports a positive vision for devolution, as set out
in the enclosed Executive Policy Statement (Appendix 1) of this
report, and agrees to work with local partners, including the
Norfolk and Suffolk Combined County Authority (NSCCA) a future
Mayor, and national partners to encourage a more ambitious,
long-term aspiration for devolution in the region.
 
2)   
That Cabinet endorses the draft Investment Prospectus, as set out
in Appendix 2, and delegates to the Chief Executive, in
consultation with the Leader, the consultation and finalisation of
a Prospectus to be shared, aiding Breckland’s engagement with
the NSCCA on support for these schemes.
 
Option 2 – Do nothing.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to support a positive vision for devolution in Norfolk and Suffolk and endorse a draft Investment Prospectus.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To approve proposed response to statutory
consultation regarding Local Government Reorganisation in Norfolk
& Suffolk
content:
RESOLVED that:
 
1)    
That Cabinet supports Breckland’s proposed approach to
responses to the statutory consultation on Local Government
Reorganisation in Norfolk and Suffolk
 
2)    
That Cabinet delegates authority to the Chief Executive, in
consultation with the Leader of the Council, to finalise and submit
Breckland Council’s response to the consultation.
 

LGR in Norfolk is the biggest
potential change to local government in over 50 years, responding
to the consultation on all proposals ensures that the views of
Breckland are contributed.
 
Breckland’s Council
supported the three unitary proposal that was submitted to
Government in September. This proposal was shaped by Breckland
Council and its partners and delivers against the factors that are
of greatest importance to our communities. This consultation
represents the final chance that Breckland Council has to feed into
the decision-making process.
 
LGR in Suffolk is also of
interest and importance to Breckland residents. Whatever the
outcome is will influence how future devolution in Norfolk &
Suffolk operates, and which councils will be constituent
members.
 

Option 1 (Recommended) – To
approve Breckland’s proposed response to the statutory
consultation on Local Government Reorganisation in Norfolk &
Suffolk. Delegating authority to the Chief Executive, in
consultation with the Leader of the Council, to finalise and submit
Breckland Council’s response to the consultation.
 
Option 2 – Do nothing
topline: The Cabinet has decided to support Breckland Council's response to the consultation on Local Government Reorganisation in Norfolk and Suffolk.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To outline the process to
implement a Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO) and seek approval
to consult on the terms of a PSPO for Dereham Town
Centre.
content:
To outline the process to
implement a Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO) and seek approval
to consult on the terms of a PSPO for Dereham Town
Centre.

RESOLVED that the Council proceeds with
the necessary consultation on the introduction of a Public Spaces
Protection Order for Dereham Town Centre.
 

The consultation exercise will assist the
Council in understanding:
 

·       
The nature and extent of specific problems caused by ongoing
activities (e.g., street drinking and associated anti-social
behaviour).

·       
What actions partner agencies may need to take to address these
issues.
 
The consultation
will help identify the type and frequency of anti-social behaviour
experienced in Dereham Town Centre.
 
Acting on the
consultation results and investigating issues raised will
demonstrate the Council’s commitment to reducing and
preventing crime and protecting the community and
environment.
 

Option 1)        Do
nothing. Not recommended. The Council should demonstrate good
practice by considering all available powers, including its
discretionary responsibility to respond to anti-social behaviour
under the Act.
 
Option 2)        Carry out the
consultation process. Recommended. Statutory consultation is
required to understand the types of complaints and issues being
experienced by residents, visitors and businesses in Dereham Town
Centre and to gather evidence to support any future PSPO. A
six-week consultation period offering both online and written
submission options is proposed.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to consult on implementing a Public Spaces Protection Order in Dereham Town Centre to address ongoing issues of anti-social behavior.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To see Cabinet approval to undertake public consultation on
the emerging Regulation 18 Local Plan: Full Update for a period of
at least 6 weeks.
content:
To see Cabinet approval to undertake public consultation on
the emerging Regulation 18 Local Plan: Full Update for a period of
at least 6 weeks.

 
Subject to the
inclusion of the agreed additional recommendations, that Officers
placed PDF maps alongside the text for each allocation in the Plan
and slight modification be made to one of the paragraphs in Chapter
12 of the Plan, it was:
 
RESOLVED THAT:
 

1)   
The Draft Local Plan (Regulation 18) set out in Appendix 1 to this
report be approved.
 

2)   
The Draft Plan included at Appendix 1 be published for consultation
for a period of at least 6 weeks.
 

3)   
Delegated authority be granted to the Director of Planning and
Building Control, in consultation with the Leader of the Council to
make any necessary typographical or other non-material changes to
Appendix 1 prior to publication for consultation.
 
 

The Draft Local Plan proposed at Appendix 1 builds on the
extensive community engagement that has been ongoing since March
2023 and sets out a full draft Local Plan that incorporates a
series of options for strategic development and preferred options
for sustainable growth across the District.
 
The preparation of a Local Plan is a statutory requirement
and must follow a statutory procedure,
including public consultation and examination. If the Council were
to pursue a different approach, overall preparation of a new Local
Plan for Breckland would be substantially delayed leading to
potential risk in the ongoing management and delivery of
development in the District. Regard also
needs to be given to proposed change in
the Local Plan process, which the Council would need to undertake
if it misses the transition date of December 2026 for submission to
the Planning Inspectorate.

Option 1: Agree the proposed Draft Local Plan included at
Appendix 1 of this report for Consultation, provide delegated
authority for minor amendments to the Plan ahead of its publication
for consultation and agree to a minimum six-week consultation
period on the Plan.
 
Option 2: Alternatively, Cabinet could decide not to
undertake consultation on the draft Local Plan included
at Appendix 1 and request substantial
amendments to the Plan or seek a different approach.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Draft Local Plan for public consultation, setting out options for strategic development and sustainable growth in the District.

decision_maker: Cllr Sarah Suggitt, Deputy Leader and Executive Member for Housing & Planning
purpose:
Introduction of Monitoring Fee for the processing of
Unilateral Undertakings for single plot self-build applications and
a title check fee.
content:
Introduction of Monitoring Fee for the processing of
Unilateral Undertakings for single plot self-build applications and
a title check fee.

Breckland Council authorises the introduction
of a Monitoring Fee for the processing of Unilateral Undertakings
(UU) for single plot self-build applications and a title check fee
to make the UU enforceable.

The cost of registering and monitoring
obligations lies with the Local Planning Authority, despite
developers and applicants benefiting from the
development.  Therefore, it is
considered that this modest contribution towards these costs would
benefit the Council financially and would go some way to covering
these costs in terms of registration and monitoring, whilst noting
costs would be significantly higher if there was a need to enforce
such a legal obligation.  The average
registering time for such agreements would be approximately two
hours, and the monitoring will depend on compliance with the
agreements, however, it is predicated that at least one check would
be made, with the average staffing cost (including on-costs)
amounting to £34.00 per hour.  On
this basis, this is a modest charge proposed and only aimed to
initial cover costs on the average agreement, whilst noting it may
not eliminate all cost, as set out above.
 
The title check fee is to cover the cost of
our legal team’s time and land search fees to undertake the
title check to ensure that the Unilateral Undertaken is
enforceable.
 


·        
To authorise the introduction of the Monitoring and Title Check
Fee.

·        
Not to permit the introduction of the Monitoring Fee and Title
Check Fee.

·        
To permit the introduction of either the Monitoring Fee or the
Title Check Fee
topline: The Deputy Leader and Executive Member for Housing & Planning has decided to introduce a Monitoring Fee and Title Check Fee for single plot self-build applications.

decision_maker: Cllr Sarah Suggitt, Deputy Leader and Executive Member for Housing & Planning
purpose:
Recommendation to update Building Control Fees

content:
Recommendation to update Building Control Fees
 
To propose an increase to
Breckland’s Building Control fees in line with rising
operational costs and Local Authority comparators, ensuring
financial sustainability, cost recovery, and continued delivery of
a competitive, high-quality service.
 

Breckland Council
authorises the introduction of an administration fee for the
processing of applications submitted via email/postal
service.
 

The comparative analysis of Building Control
service costs has highlighted that Breckland’s current fee
structure is not aligned with the rising operational costs and
market trends.
 
As detailed in Appendix C (attached), the
proposed fee increases will bring Breckland’s fees more in
line with those of neighbouring authorities, while still
maintaining a competitive position. These adjustments, particularly
in light of the proposed hourly rate increase and
application-specific fee changes, are crucial to ensure that the
service remains financially sustainable and capable of delivering
high-quality regulatory oversight.
 
The proposed increases, as outlined in
Appendices B and C (attached), will provide a necessary boost to
income, helping to cover rising operational costs and ensuring
continued service effectiveness.
 
With the right communication and gradual
implementation, these fee adjustments will help maintain
Breckland's position in the market, while supporting its long-term
viability.
 


·        
To raise the Building Control fees accordingly.
 

·        
Not to raise the Building Control fees.
topline: The Deputy Leader and Executive Member for Housing & Planning has decided to propose an increase in Breckland's Building Control fees to ensure financial sustainability and competitiveness.
